# Agentic ODI [![CI](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/alehar9320/agentic-odi/branch/main/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/alehar9320/agentic-odi) [![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10%2B-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/downloads/) [![uv](https://img.shields.io/badge/uv-managed-green)](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) [![Ruff](https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/astral-sh/ruff/main/assets/badge/v2.json)](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff) [![FastMCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastMCP-powered-orange)](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp) [![pytest](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-pytest-blue)](https://pytest.org) [![MCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/Model%20Context%20Protocol-enabled-8A2BE2)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) > **[![Experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/Experimental-1e293b?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi)** > **Experimental test to learn and evaluate the feasibility of utilizing Model Context Protocol (MCP) for Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI) specifications.**
--- **Agentic ODI** explores how the [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) can turn [Outcome-Driven Innovation](https://strategyn.com/outcome-driven-innovation/) into a live, agent-queryable source of context. Instead of feeding LLMs disconnected prompts, an MCP-powered ODI server acts as the "brain" of customer needs — letting agents invent, evaluate, and ideate solutions anchored in verified, measurable customer outcomes (Job Maps, Desired Outcomes, and Opportunity Scores). This repository is an experimental testbed for understanding server–client MCP communication streams, built on [`FastMCP`](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp). We don't publish dates. This page changes when the code does. ## Code Overview A [uv workspace](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/workspaces/) of six installable Python projects plus the React `studio/` front end, each with its own build, tests, and layout: | Package | Description | |---|---| | **`core/`** (`agentic-odi-core`) | Domain models, the `ODIService` business-logic layer, and repository implementations (in-memory and SQLite), including ODI opportunity-score computation. | | **`mcp_server/`** (`agentic-odi-mcp-server`) | A foundational MCP Server exposing an HTTP transport layer. It hosts tools for Jobs, Steps, Desired Outcomes, and Customer Outcomes (linking customer value to business value). | | **`local_server/`** (`agentic-odi-local-server`) | The FastAPI **Living Studio sidecar**. It talks to the MCP server on the client's behalf and serves the Studio API — configuration, health probes, canvas data, MCP mutations, and streaming (SSE) chat with the LLM tool-loop — plus the built SPA when `studio/dist` exists. | | **`client/`** (`agentic-odi-client`) | The local dev **launcher** (`run.py` / `python -m client.run`) that starts the MCP server and the Studio sidecar together. | | **`studio/`** (React + TypeScript + Vite) | **The Living Studio** front end — a spatial, conversational GUI for Outcome-Driven Innovation with an interactive Opportunity Landscape, Universal Job Map, WYSIWYG Impact Simulation, and Causal Lineage inspection, paired with an autonomous copilot. Ships as a browser SPA and as a **Tauri 2 desktop app** (`studio/src-tauri/`). | | **`cli/`** (`agentic-odi-cli`) | A [`Typer`](https://github.com/fastapi/typer)-based command-line interface with an interactive chat mode plus `version`, `update`, `connectors`, and `customer-outcomes` (alias `outcomes`) commands. Data commands are local-first (`--backend local`, default) or remote (`--backend mcp`), with readable tables, `--json`, and a top-level `score`. | | **`connectors/`** (`agentic-odi-connectors`) | Pluggable external integrations. The first kind is an **MCP client connector** that connects to a remote MCP server over HTTP, checks health, and ingests tools/resources into a local ingest sink. Additional kinds (REST, webhooks, and so on) can register against the same protocol later. | ## Quick Start **Prerequisites:** Python 3.10+ and the [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) package manager. ```bash # Install the entire workspace (all six projects plus dev tooling) uv sync --all-packages # Build the Studio SPA, then launch the MCP server and Living Studio together npm --prefix studio run build python -m client.run ``` | Service | URL | |---|---| | MCP Server | http://localhost:8000/mcp | | The Living Studio | http://127.0.0.1:8100 | For hot reload, `npm --prefix studio run dev:full` starts the MCP server, the sidecar, and Vite together on http://localhost:5173. For the desktop app, use `npm --prefix studio run tauri dev`. See [Running The Living Studio](docs/living-studio.md). The Studio needs an OpenAI-compatible LLM with tool-calling support to drive its agent — see the [Local LLM Backend](docs/local-llm.md). ### CLI at a glance The CLI is local-first, so data commands work without a running server: ```bash python -m cli --version # print the Agentic ODI version python -m cli --help # show available options and commands python -m cli # start interactive chat in a terminal agentic-odi customer-outcomes list agentic-odi score 8 2 # ODI opportunity score → 14.00 ``` Add `--backend mcp` to route data commands through a running MCP server (`python -m mcp_server`). See the [CLI Reference](docs/cli.md). ### Install the binary Prebuilt binaries are available for Linux, macOS, and Windows: ```bash curl -fsSL https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh ```

## Skill Priority

When multiple skills apply, process skills come first — they set the approach, then implementation skills (frontend-design, etc.) carry it out. Brainstorming and systematic-debugging are Superpowers' most common process skills, but the rule holds for any of them.

- "Fix this bug" → superpowers:systematic-debugging first, then domain skills.

## User Instructions

User instructions (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md, etc, direct requests) take precedence over skills, which in turn override default behavior. Only skip skill workflows or instructions when your human partner has explicitly told you to.

## Freebuff Tool Mapping

Skills speak in actions, not tool names. On Freebuff they resolve as follows:

| Action skills request | Freebuff equivalent |
| --- | --- |
| Invoke or load a skill | `skill` with the skill directory name (for example `{"name": "brainstorming"}`) |

For a second pair of eyes, use the `requesting-code-review` reviewer prompt as a structured self-review, or ask your human partner to start a fresh session. |

Freebuff discovers project skills in `.agents/skills/*/SKILL.md` and lists each skill's name and description in the system prompt. Load one by name with the `skill` tool; reading a `SKILL.md` with `read_files` is only a fallback if the tool fails.

    async def health(self) -> HealthStatus:

- **External connectors**: Integrations live in the `connectors/` workspace package. New kinds implement `connectors.protocol.Connector` and register via `register_kind`. Do not write ingested records into `jobs_db` / outcomes unless a later mapping task says so.
- **MCP client vs ODI server**: The ODI FastMCP **server** exposes product tools. The MCP **client connector** uses `fastmcp.Client` over HTTP to ingest data from *external* MCP servers. Prefer in-memory `Client(server)` tests for that connector, same as server tests.

### 5. Testing Strategy (FastMCP)
- **First-Class Documentation**: Treat tests as living documentation that demonstrate how features work while protecting against regressions.
- **Speed & Isolation**: Tests must be fast (< 1s) and self-contained. Use `@pytest.mark.integration` or `@pytest.mark.client_process` for slower, integration, or resource-dependent tests.
- **Structure**: This repo is a uv workspace. Mirror each project's code structure in its own `tests/` directory (e.g., `mcp_server/src/mcp_server/mcp_server.py` -> `mcp_server/tests/test_server_tools.py`, `connectors/src/connectors/mcp/connector.py` -> `connectors/tests/test_mcp_connector.py`).
- **Atomic Tests**: Each test must verify exactly one specific behavior with clear intent in test names and assertions. Avoid multi-behavior tests.
- **In-Memory Testing (Preferred)**: Favor testing functionality deterministically by passing the `FastMCP` server directly into the `Client(server)` instance. This runs in-memory without network overhead for deterministic and lightning-fast execution.
- **Transport Testing (When Needed)**: For HTTP/SSE network transport tests, prefer the isolated in-process `fastmcp.utilities.tests.run_server_async(server)` context manager over subprocess testing (which uses `run_server_in_process` and is slower to debug).
- **Data Assertions**: Utilize `inline-snapshot` (`snapshot()`) for assessing complex data structures like tool API JSON schemas or expected responses.

display.text:
"""Shared Pydantic models for external connectors and ingest records."""

from __future__ import annotations

import uuid
from typing import Any, Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

ItemType = Literal["resource", "tool_result", "catalog"]
McpAuthMode = Literal["none", "oauth"]
EvidenceItemType = Literal["catalog", "resource", "tool_result", "manual", "note"]


class HealthStatus(BaseModel):
    ok: bool
    message: str
    details: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)


class IngestRecord(BaseModel):
    id: str = Field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4()))
    source_name: str
    source_kind: str
    item_type: ItemType
    name: str
    content: str
    raw: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)


class IngestBatch(BaseModel):
    connector_name: str
    records: list[IngestRecord] = Field(default_factory=list)
    errors: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)


class McpConnectorSettings(BaseModel):
    """Connection details for an MCP server.

    ``url`` and ``headers`` may interpolate environment variables with
    ``${VAR}`` so registry files never hold tokens. ``env_vars`` names the
    variables that must be present before connecting.
    """

    url: str
    tools: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    auth: McpAuthMode = "none"
    headers: dict[str, str] = Field(default_factory=dict)
    env_vars: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)


class RestConnectorSettings(BaseModel):
    url: str
    method: Literal["GET", "POST"] = "GET"
    headers: dict[str, str] = Field(default_factory=dict)
    json_body: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    records_key: str | None = None
    timeout: float = 10.0
    item_type: ItemType = "resource"


class ConnectorConfig(BaseModel):
    name: str
    kind: str
    enabled: bool = True
    settings: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)

4: MCP server: the endpoint, how it authenticates, and where its documentation
5: lives. Presets are grouped by the five capability areas an outcome-driven
6: innovation process needs, so a new workspace can be wired up with
7: ``agentic-odi connectors add mcp --preset <id>`` instead of hunting for URLs.
8: """

20:     "voice-of-customer",
21:     "quantitative-data",
22:     "market-intelligence",
23:     "strategy-alignment",
24:     "knowledge-output",
25: ]

Each preset captures everything needed to register a connector for a well-known
MCP server: the endpoint, how it authenticates, and where its documentation
lives. Presets are grouped by the five capability areas an outcome-driven
innovation process needs, so a new workspace can be wired up with
``agentic-odi connectors add mcp --preset <id>`` instead of hunting for URLs.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from typing import Any, Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from agentic_odi_connectors.models import ConnectorConfig

CapabilityArea = Literal[
    "voice-of-customer",
    "quantitative-data",
    "market-intelligence",
    "strategy-alignment",
    "knowledge-output",
]

AREA_LABELS: dict[CapabilityArea, str] = {
    "voice-of-customer": "Voice of customer & qualitative research",
    "quantitative-data": "Quantitative data & opportunity scoring",
    "market-intelligence": "Market & competitive intelligence",
    "strategy-alignment": "Product strategy & backlog alignment",
    "knowledge-output": "Strategy & knowledge management output",
}

ENV_VAR_PATTERN = re.compile(r"\$\{([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\}")


class UnknownPresetError(ValueError):
    def __init__(self, preset_id: str) -> None:
        self.preset_id = preset_id
        super().__init__(f"Unknown preset: {preset_id} (try 'agentic-odi connectors catalog')")


class UnknownAreaError(ValueError):
    def __init__(self, area: str) -> None:
        self.area = area
        valid = ", ".join(AREA_LABELS)
        super().__init__(f"Unknown capability area: {area} (expected one of: {valid})")


class ConnectorPreset(BaseModel):
    """A known MCP server plus the credentials it needs."""

    id: str
    label: str
    area: CapabilityArea
    summary: str
    url: str
    auth: Literal["none", "oauth"] = "none"
    env_vars: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    headers: dict[str, str] = Field(default_factory=dict)
    docs: str
    tools: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)

    def referenced_env_vars(self) -> set[str]:
        """Environment variables the URL or headers interpolate with ``${VAR}``."""
        found: set[str] = set()
        for value in [self.url, *self.headers.values()]:
            found.update(ENV_VAR_PATTERN.findall(value))
        return found


PRESETS: tuple[ConnectorPreset, ...] = (
    # 1. Voice of customer & qualitative research
    ConnectorPreset(
        id="notion",
        label="Notion",
        area="voice-of-customer",
        summary="Interview notes, feedback logs, and PRDs from Notion pages.",
        url="https://mcp.notion.com/mcp",
        auth="oauth",
        docs="https://developers.notion.com/docs/mcp",
    ),
    ConnectorPreset(
        id="gong",

        area="voice-of-customer",
        summary="Sales and success call transcripts with direct customer quotes.",
        url="https://mcp.gong.io/mcp",
        auth="oauth",
        docs="https://help.gong.io/",
    ),
    ConnectorPreset(
        id="fireflies",
        label="Fireflies.ai",
        area="voice-of-customer",
        summary="Meeting transcripts and summaries for unmet-need mining.",
        url="https://mcp.fireflies.ai/mcp",
        auth="oauth",
        docs="https://docs.fireflies.ai/",
    ),
    ConnectorPreset(
        id="intercom",
        label="Intercom",
        area="voice-of-customer",
        summary="Support conversations and recurring customer frustrations.",
        url="https://mcp.intercom.com/mcp",
        auth="oauth",
        docs="https://developers.intercom.com/docs/guides/mcp",
    ),
    ConnectorPreset(
        id="confluence",
        label="Atlassian Confluence",
        area="voice-of-customer",
        summary="Existing PRDs, research write-ups, and product documentation.",
        url="https://mcp.atlassian.com/v1/mcp",
        auth="oauth",
        docs="https://www.atlassian.com/platform/remote-mcp-server",
    ),
    # 2. Quantitative data & opportunity scoring
    ConnectorPreset(
        id="posthog",
        label="PostHog",
        area="quantitative-data",
        summary="Feature usage, funnels, and drop-off rates for outcome scoring.",
        url="https://mcp.posthog.com/mcp",
        auth="oauth",
        docs="https://posthog.com/docs/model-context-protocol",
    ),
    ConnectorPreset(
        id="amplitude",
        label="Amplitude",
        area="quantitative-data",
        summary="Behavioral cohorts and adoption metrics behind each outcome.",
        url="https://mcp.amplitude.com/mcp",
        auth="oauth",
        docs="https://amplitude.com/docs/amplitude-ai/amplitude-mcp",
    ),
    ConnectorPreset(
        id="mixpanel",
        label="Mixpanel",
        area="quantitative-data",
        summary="Event analytics for importance and satisfaction evidence.",
        url="https://mcp.mixpanel.com/mcp",
        auth="oauth",
        docs="https://docs.mixpanel.com/docs/mcp",
    ),
    # 3. Market & competitive intelligence
    ConnectorPreset(
        id="exa",
        label="Exa",
        area="market-intelligence",
        summary="Semantic web search for competitor launches and market gaps.",
        url="https://mcp.exa.ai/mcp?exaApiKey=${EXA_API_KEY}",
        env_vars=["EXA_API_KEY"],
        docs="https://docs.exa.ai/reference/exa-mcp",
    ),
    ConnectorPreset(
        id="tavily",

        docs=(
            "https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/customizing-copilot/"
            "using-model-context-protocol/extending-copilot-chat-with-mcp"
        ),
    ),
    ConnectorPreset(
        id="jira",
        label="Atlassian Jira",
        area="strategy-alignment",
        summary="Epics and issues to align delivery work with desired outcomes.",
        url="https://mcp.atlassian.com/v1/mcp",

        id="miro",
        label="Miro",
        area="strategy-alignment",
        summary="Outcome matrices and customer journey maps on a shared board.",
        url="https://mcp.miro.com/",
        auth="oauth",
        docs="https://developers.miro.com/docs/miro-mcp",
    ),
    ConnectorPreset(
        id="figma",
        label="Figma",
        area="strategy-alignment",
        summary="FigJam maps and design context for outcome workshops.",
        url="https://mcp.figma.com/mcp",
        auth="oauth",
        docs="https://developers.figma.com/docs/figma-mcp-server/",
    ),
    # 5. Strategy & knowledge management output
    ConnectorPreset(
        id="slack",
        label="Slack",
        area="knowledge-output",
        summary="Post opportunity-score digests and JTBD insights to channels.",
        url="https://mcp.slack.com/mcp",
        auth="oauth",
        docs="https://docs.slack.dev/ai/",
    ),
)


def list_presets(area: str | None = None) -> list[ConnectorPreset]:
    """Return presets, optionally filtered by capability area."""
    if area is None:
        return list(PRESETS)
    if area not in AREA_LABELS:
        raise UnknownAreaError(area)
    return [preset for preset in PRESETS if preset.area == area]


def get_preset(preset_id: str) -> ConnectorPreset:
    for preset in PRESETS:
        if preset.id == preset_id:
            return preset
    raise UnknownPresetError(preset_id)


def connector_config_from_preset(
    preset: ConnectorPreset,
    *,
    name: str | None = None,
    url: str | None = None,
    tools: list[str] | None = None,
    enabled: bool = True,
) -> ConnectorConfig:
    """Build a registry entry from a preset, allowing local overrides."""
    settings: dict[str, Any] = {
        "url": url or preset.url,
        "auth": preset.auth,
        "headers": dict(preset.headers),
        "env_vars": list(preset.env_vars),
        "tools": list(tools if tools is not None else preset.tools),
    }
    return ConnectorConfig(
        name=name or preset.id,
        kind="mcp",
        enabled=enabled,
        settings=settings,
    )


__all__ = [
    "AREA_LABELS",
    "ENV_VAR_PATTERN",
    "PRESETS",
    "CapabilityArea",
    "ConnectorPreset",
    "UnknownAreaError",
    "UnknownPresetError",
    "connector_config_from_preset",
    "get_preset",
    "list_presets",
]

# External Connectors (MCP Ingest)

Connectors are named integrations stored in `.agentic-odi/connectors.json` (or a
path you pass with `--config` / `AGENTIC_ODI_CONNECTORS_FILE`). The first kind is
`mcp`: Agentic ODI acts as an MCP **client** and pulls catalog, resources, and
optional tool results from an external MCP **server**.

## Presets

The fastest way to connect is a preset. `connectors catalog` lists every
built-in preset, grouped by the capability area it serves:

```bash
python -m cli connectors catalog                          # all presets
python -m cli connectors catalog --area strategy-alignment
python -m cli connectors catalog --json
```

| Capability area (`--area`) | Presets |
|---|---|
| Voice of customer & qualitative research (`voice-of-customer`) | `notion`, `gong`, `fireflies`, `intercom`, `confluence` |
| Quantitative data & opportunity scoring (`quantitative-data`) | `posthog`, `amplitude`, `mixpanel` |
| Market & competitive intelligence (`market-intelligence`) | `exa`, `tavily` |
| Product strategy & backlog alignment (`strategy-alignment`) | `linear`, `github`, `jira`, `miro`, `figma` |
| Strategy & knowledge management output (`knowledge-output`) | `slack` |

Register one with `--preset`; `--name` defaults to the preset id:

```bash
# Token-based preset: export the variable it needs first
export GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN=ghp_...
python -m cli connectors add mcp --preset github
python -m cli connectors health --name github
python -m cli connectors ingest --name github

# OAuth-based preset: the browser consent flow starts on first use
python -m cli connectors add mcp --preset notion
```

Credentials never enter the registry. Presets that use API keys store `${VAR}`
placeholders that are resolved from the environment when a connection is
opened, and `connectors health` names any variable that is missing. `--url`
overrides the endpoint (self-hosted or proxied deployments) and `--tool` still
selects which tools to call during ingest.

Custom servers keep working the same way:

```bash
python -m cli connectors add mcp --name internal --url https://mcp.internal.example/mcp --tool latest_quote
python -m cli connectors list
```

> [!NOTE]
> Presets cover MCP servers with a hosted endpoint. Servers you run yourself
> (Snowflake, BigQuery, Google Drive, Brave Search, and similar) are added with
> an explicit `--url`. The catalog lives in
> `connectors/src/connectors/catalog.py`.

> [!NOTE]
> OAuth tokens are cached in memory for the life of one CLI process, so an OAuth
> preset may ask for consent again on the next `connectors health` or
> `connectors ingest`. Prefer a token-based preset where the server offers one.

## Ingest behavior

Ingested records are normalized (`catalog`, `resource`, `tool_result`) and
appended to the in-process ingest sink. They are **not** written into the ODI
jobs/outcomes store — mapping ingested evidence onto ODI artifacts is still on
the [roadmap](roadmap.md).

Additional kinds (REST, webhooks, and so on) can register against the same
`Connector` protocol later.

1: # Running The Living Studio
2: 
3: **The Living Studio** is the conversational GUI for Outcome-Driven Innovation:
4: an interactive Opportunity Landscape, Universal Job Map, WYSIWYG Impact
5: Simulation, and Causal Lineage inspection, paired with an autonomous agent
6: connected to the MCP server.
7: 
8: The Studio runs three ways. All of them serve the same SPA, which talks only to
9: the sidecar on `http://127.0.0.1:8100` — the SPA never contacts MCP or the LLM
10: directly.
11: 
12: ## Architecture
13: 
14: ```text
15: ┌────────────────────────────┐  /api (JSON)  ┌───────────────────────────────┐
16: │  Living Studio SPA         │ ────────────▶ │  local_server (sidecar)       │
17: │  React + TS + Vite         │  /api/chat    │  FastAPI on 127.0.0.1:8100    │
18: │  (browser or Tauri webview)│ ◀──────────── │  - config / health / canvas   │
19: └────────────────────────────┘  SSE stream   │  - steps / outcomes (via MCP) │
20:                                              │  - /api/chat (LLM tool-loop)  │
21:                                              └───────────────┬───────────────┘
22:                                                              │ MCP (HTTP)
23:                                                              ▼
24:                                              ┌───────────────────────────────┐

# Running The Living Studio

**The Living Studio** is the conversational GUI for Outcome-Driven Innovation:
an interactive Opportunity Landscape, Universal Job Map, WYSIWYG Impact
Simulation, and Causal Lineage inspection, paired with an autonomous agent
connected to the MCP server.

The Studio runs three ways. All of them serve the same SPA, which talks only to
the sidecar on `http://127.0.0.1:8100` — the SPA never contacts MCP or the LLM
directly.

## Architecture

```text
┌────────────────────────────┐  /api (JSON)  ┌───────────────────────────────┐
│  Living Studio SPA         │ ────────────▶ │  local_server (sidecar)       │
│  React + TS + Vite         │  /api/chat    │  FastAPI on 127.0.0.1:8100    │
│  (browser or Tauri webview)│ ◀──────────── │  - config / health / canvas   │
└────────────────────────────┘  SSE stream   │  - steps / outcomes (via MCP) │
                                             │  - /api/chat (LLM tool-loop)  │
                                             └───────────────┬───────────────┘
                                                             │ MCP (HTTP)
                                                             ▼
                                             ┌───────────────────────────────┐
                                             │  mcp_server  :8000/mcp        │
                                             └───────────────────────────────┘
                                                             ▲
                                                             │ OpenAI-compatible
                                             ┌───────────────┴───────────────┐
                                             │  Your local LLM backend       │
                                             └───────────────────────────────┘
```

## 1. Web — production build (recommended for a quick look)

```bash
npm --prefix studio run build   # build the SPA into studio/dist
python -m client.run            # starts MCP :8000 + sidecar :8100
```

| Service | URL |
|---|---|
| MCP Server | http://localhost:8000/mcp |
| Living Studio | http://127.0.0.1:8100 |

`python -m client.run` starts both processes concurrently; press **Ctrl+C** to
stop both.

## 2. Web — dev with hot reload

Vite proxies `/api` to the sidecar:

```bash
npm --prefix studio run dev:full   # MCP + sidecar + Vite together
# open http://localhost:5173
```

## 3. Desktop — Tauri 2

The app spawns the MCP server and sidecar itself:

```bash
npm --prefix studio run tauri dev     # dev window
npm --prefix studio run tauri build   # bundles: .deb / .AppImage (Linux), .app / .dmg (macOS), .msi / .exe (Windows)
```

> [!NOTE]
> **Tauri prerequisites.** The desktop build needs the WebKitGTK toolchain and
> Rust 1.90+. On Debian/Ubuntu:
>
> ```bash
> sudo apt-get install -y libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev build-essential pkg-config curl wget file \
>   libxdo-dev libssl-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev patchelf xdg-utils libfuse2t64
> ```
>
> The Tauri CLI ships as the `@tauri-apps/cli` npm dev dependency
> (`npm --prefix studio run tauri`). The sidecar is launched with
> `uv run python -m …` from the repository root; if the app cannot locate the
> repo root, set `AGENTIC_ODI_REPO_ROOT`.

## Desktop signing & updater secrets

Self-updating and code signing are **env-driven**: if a secret is absent, an
unsigned artifact is produced instead of failing. CI reads these from GitHub
Actions secrets.

| Secret | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` | Signs updater artifacts (`.sig`) and the `latest.json` manifest. A tagged release fails loudly without it. Generate with `npm --prefix studio run tauri signer generate`. |
| `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD` | Password for the private key (optional when the key has none). |
| `APPLE_CERTIFICATE` / `APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` | macOS Developer ID certificate (base64 `.p12`) and its password. |
| `APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY` | macOS signing identity. |
| `APPLE_ID` / `APPLE_PASSWORD` / `APPLE_TEAM_ID` | macOS notarization credentials. |
| `WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE` / `WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` | Windows Authenticode PFX (base64) and its password; imported by CI and injected into the bundle config. |

Releases are published by `.github/workflows/tauri-release.yml` when a `v*` tag
is pushed. The desktop app checks for updates on startup and via
**Settings → Check for updates**.

### Managing the updater signing key

The updater key pair authenticates release artifacts so an installed app can
verify that an auto-update genuinely came from you. The **public** key is
embedded in `studio/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` (`plugins.updater.pubkey`) and is
safe to commit. The **private** key must never be committed, logged, printed in
CI, or attached to a build artifact.

1. **Generate a key pair** (only if you need a new one). Leave `-p ""` for a
   passwordless key, or pass a password and remember it:

   ```bash
   npm --prefix studio run tauri signer generate -- -w ./living-studio.key -p "" -f
   ```

   This writes `living-studio.key` (private, `0600`) and `living-studio.key.pub`
   (public).

2. **Paste the public key** into `studio/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`:

   ```jsonc
   {
     "plugins": {
       "updater": {
         "endpoints": ["https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/releases/latest/download/latest.json"],
         "pubkey": "<contents of living-studio.key.pub>"
       }
     }
   }
   ```

3. **Store the private key outside the repository** (the repo root is
   git-tracked; a sibling directory is not), with restricted permissions:

   ```bash
   mkdir -p ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys && chmod 700 ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys
   mv living-studio.key ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys/
   chmod 600 ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys/living-studio.key
   ```

   Move it to a long-term secret store (password manager, 1Password/Bitwarden/
   Vault, or a private encrypted backup) when you decide where that lives.
   Losing it means future releases can no longer be signed for existing
   installs.

4. **Add the private key as a GitHub Actions secret** (Settings → Secrets and
   variables → Actions → New repository secret), or via the CLI:

   ```bash
   gh secret set TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY < ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys/living-studio.key
   gh secret set TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD --body ""   # only if you set a password
   ```

5. **Verify** the secrets exist (values are never displayed):

   ```bash
   gh secret list
   ```

6. **Rotate** by repeating steps 1–4, then publishing a release signed with the
   new key. Existing installs still verify against the public key compiled into
   their binary, so keep the old private key usable and publish the new public
   key ahead of the cut-over.

> [!CAUTION]
> If the private key leaks, treat auto-updates as compromised: generate a new
> pair, rotate the Actions secret, and publish a freshly signed release.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Migration note.** The Streamlit UI (`client/src/client/app.py`) has been
> removed. The Living Studio now lives in `studio/` (browser SPA + Tauri desktop
> app) and is served by the `local_server` sidecar on port **8100** (previously
> Streamlit's `8501`). Start everything with `python -m client.run`. All
> `AGENTIC_ODI_*` environment variable names, the demo dataset, and the ODI
> formulas are unchanged.

## Connecting an LLM

The Studio needs an OpenAI-compatible LLM backend with tool-calling support to
drive the agent. For a fully local setup, see
[Local LLM Backend](local-llm.md).

## Agent-Driven Testing

Type `/dev` in the AI assistant to trigger the full automated workflow: it starts
both processes, opens the browser, sends a test message, and reports the results.

Type `/test` to have the agent run all tests and report the results
automatically.

"""Connection probing and LLM health checks, ported from the Streamlit app."""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import os
import socket
from urllib.parse import urlparse

from openai import AsyncOpenAI

DEFAULT_BASE_URL = "http://localhost:8001/v1"
DEFAULT_API_KEY = "local"
DEFAULT_MODEL = "local-tools-model"
DEFAULT_MCP_URL = "http://localhost:8000/mcp"

OFFLINE_MESSAGE = "LLM server offline (Local Studio Mode enabled)"


def _load_profile_fallback() -> dict[str, str]:
    """Read llm_profile.json directly without importing cli package."""
    import json
    from pathlib import Path

    xdg = os.getenv("XDG_CONFIG_HOME")
    cfg_dir = Path(xdg) / "agentic-odi" if xdg else Path.home() / ".config" / "agentic-odi"
    profile_file = cfg_dir / "llm_profile.json"
    if not profile_file.exists():
        return {}
    try:
        with open(profile_file) as f:
            return json.load(f)
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
        return {}


def defaults() -> dict[str, str]:
    """Streamlit-compatible environment defaults (same variable names).

    Priority order: environment variable > persisted llm_profile.json > hardcoded constant.
    """
    profile = _load_profile_fallback()
    return {
        "base_url": os.getenv("AGENTIC_ODI_BASE_URL")
        or profile.get("base_url")
        or DEFAULT_BASE_URL,
        "api_key": os.getenv("AGENTIC_ODI_API_KEY") or profile.get("api_key") or DEFAULT_API_KEY,
        "model_name": os.getenv("AGENTIC_ODI_MODEL") or profile.get("model") or DEFAULT_MODEL,
        "mcp_url": os.getenv("AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL") or profile.get("mcp_url") or DEFAULT_MCP_URL,
    }


def is_endpoint_reachable(url: str, timeout: float = 0.3) -> bool:
    """Quick socket check to verify a port is open without hanging on HTTP reads."""
    try:
        parsed = urlparse(url)
        host = parsed.hostname or "localhost"
        port = parsed.port or (443 if parsed.scheme == "https" else 80)
        with socket.create_connection((host, port), timeout=timeout):
            return True
    except OSError:
        return False


def classify_llm_error(exc: Exception) -> tuple[str, str]:
    message = str(exc)
    lower = message.lower()
    connection_indicators = [
        "connection error",
        "connection aborted",
        "failed to establish a new connection",
        "timed out",
        "timeout",
        "connection refused",
    ]
    if any(indicator in lower for indicator in connection_indicators):
        return "connection_error", message
    return "error", message


async def check_llm_health(base_url: str, api_key: str, model_name: str) -> tuple[bool, str]:
    """Non-blocking LLM health probe with an instant socket pre-check."""
    if not is_endpoint_reachable(base_url, timeout=0.3):
        return False, OFFLINE_MESSAGE

    client = AsyncOpenAI(base_url=base_url, api_key=api_key, timeout=1.2)
    try:
        await asyncio.wait_for(client.models.list(), timeout=1.2)
        return True, "LLM backend is reachable."
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        status, detail = classify_llm_error(exc)
        return False, f"{status}: {detail}"

"""MCP hydration and passthrough writes, ported from the Streamlit app."""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import json
import logging
from typing import Any

from agentic_odi_core import ODIService, ToolName
from fastapi import HTTPException
from fastmcp import Client as McpClient

from agentic_odi_studio_api.studio.probes import is_endpoint_reachable
from agentic_odi_studio_api.studio.seed import seed_payload

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

MCP_CALL_TIMEOUT = 3.0


async def fetch_canvas(mcp_url: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Fetch live canvas data from FastMCP, falling back to the seed prototype."""
    jobs: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    outcomes: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    steps: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    warnings: list[str] = []

    if not is_endpoint_reachable(mcp_url, timeout=0.3):
        log.warning("MCP endpoint unreachable at %s — falling back to seed data", mcp_url)
        return {**seed_payload(), "source": "seed", "warnings": ["MCP endpoint unreachable"]}

    try:
        mcp_client = McpClient(mcp_url)
        async with mcp_client:
            raw_jobs = await asyncio.wait_for(
                mcp_client.call_tool(ToolName.GET_JOBS.value, {}), timeout=1.5
            )
            try:
                parsed_jobs = json.loads(str(raw_jobs))
                if isinstance(parsed_jobs, list):
                    jobs = parsed_jobs
            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
                log.warning("Failed to parse jobs from MCP: %s", exc)
                jobs = []

            for job in jobs:
                job_id = job.get("id")
                if not job_id:
                    continue

                try:
                    raw_steps = await asyncio.wait_for(
                        mcp_client.call_tool(ToolName.GET_JOB_MAP.value, {"job_id": job_id}),
                        timeout=1.0,
                    )
                    parsed_steps = json.loads(str(raw_steps))
                    if isinstance(parsed_steps, list):
                        steps.extend(parsed_steps)
                except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
                    msg = f"Failed to fetch steps for job {job_id}: {exc}"
                    log.warning(msg)
                    warnings.append(msg)

                try:
                    raw_outcomes = await asyncio.wait_for(
                        mcp_client.call_tool(ToolName.GET_OUTCOMES.value, {"job_id": job_id}),
                        timeout=1.0,
                    )
                    parsed_outcomes = json.loads(str(raw_outcomes))
                    if isinstance(parsed_outcomes, list):
                        outcomes.extend(parsed_outcomes)
                except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
                    msg = f"Failed to fetch outcomes for job {job_id}: {exc}"
                    log.warning(msg)
                    warnings.append(msg)
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        log.warning("MCP canvas hydration failed entirely: %s", exc)
        warnings.append(f"MCP hydration error: {exc}")

    if not jobs:
        return {**seed_payload(), "source": "seed", "warnings": ["No jobs returned from MCP"]}

    return {
        "jobs": jobs,
        "steps": steps,
        "outcomes": outcomes,
        "source": "mcp",
        "warnings": warnings,
    }


def fetch_local_canvas(service: ODIService) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Read the canvas directly from the local service, no HTTP round trip."""
    jobs = [job.model_dump() for job in service.get_jobs()]
    steps: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    outcomes: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for job in jobs:
        job_id = job["id"]
        steps.extend(step.model_dump() for step in service.get_job_map(job_id))
        outcomes.extend(outcome.model_dump() for outcome in service.get_outcomes(job_id))
    return {"jobs": jobs, "steps": steps, "outcomes": outcomes, "source": "local"}


async def call_mcp_tool(mcp_url: str, tool: str, arguments: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    """Invoke an MCP tool, surfacing failures as HTTP 502."""
    if not is_endpoint_reachable(mcp_url, timeout=0.3):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=502, detail=f"MCP server unreachable at {mcp_url}")

    try:
        async with McpClient(mcp_url) as mcp_client:
            result = await asyncio.wait_for(
                mcp_client.call_tool(tool, arguments), timeout=MCP_CALL_TIMEOUT
            )
            return str(result)
    except HTTPException:
        raise
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        raise HTTPException(status_code=502, detail=f"Error calling {tool}: {exc}") from exc

from pathlib import Path

import pytest
from agentic_odi_connectors.models import ConnectorConfig
from agentic_odi_connectors.registry import (
    ConnectorNotFoundError,
    ConnectorRegistry,
    DuplicateConnectorError,
    UnknownConnectorKindError,
)


def _registry(tmp_path: Path) -> ConnectorRegistry:
    return ConnectorRegistry(tmp_path / "connectors.json")


def test_add_persists_connector(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    registry = _registry(tmp_path)
    config = ConnectorConfig(
        name="gong",
        kind="mcp",
        settings={"url": "http://localhost:9000/mcp"},
    )

    registry.add(config)

    stored = registry.list_all()
    assert len(stored) == 1
    assert stored[0].name == "gong"
    assert stored[0].kind == "mcp"
    assert stored[0].settings["url"] == "http://localhost:9000/mcp"


def test_list_returns_added_connectors(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    registry = _registry(tmp_path)
    registry.add(
        ConnectorConfig(name="one", kind="mcp", settings={"url": "http://localhost:1/mcp"})
    )
    registry.add(
        ConnectorConfig(name="two", kind="mcp", settings={"url": "http://localhost:2/mcp"})
    )

    names = {item.name for item in registry.list_all()}

    assert names == {"one", "two"}


def test_add_rejects_duplicate_name(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    registry = _registry(tmp_path)
    config = ConnectorConfig(name="gong", kind="mcp", settings={"url": "http://localhost:1/mcp"})
    registry.add(config)

    with pytest.raises(DuplicateConnectorError):
        registry.add(config)


def test_add_rejects_unknown_kind(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    registry = _registry(tmp_path)

    with pytest.raises(UnknownConnectorKindError) as exc_info:
        registry.add(ConnectorConfig(name="jira", kind="salesforce", settings={}))

    assert exc_info.value.kind == "salesforce"


def test_get_returns_matching_connector(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    registry = _registry(tmp_path)
    registry.add(
        ConnectorConfig(name="gong", kind="mcp", settings={"url": "http://localhost:1/mcp"})
    )

    found = registry.get("gong")

    assert found.name == "gong"


def test_get_missing_raises(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    registry = _registry(tmp_path)

    with pytest.raises(ConnectorNotFoundError):
        registry.get("missing")


def test_load_roundtrip(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    path = tmp_path / "connectors.json"
    first = ConnectorRegistry(path)
    first.add(ConnectorConfig(name="gong", kind="mcp", settings={"url": "http://localhost:1/mcp"}))

    second = ConnectorRegistry(path)
    loaded = second.list_all()

    assert len(loaded) == 1
    assert loaded[0].name == "gong"

<skill_content name="brainstorming">
# Skill: brainstorming

# Brainstorming

You are very good at building. You build what you believe your human
partner wants, and that belief is usually thinner than it feels. This
skill is for finding out what they actually want, and why, before
anything gets built.

People often haven't finished working out what they want. Good questions
help them think it through. When you understand the why, you make the
hundred decisions they never mention the way they would have made them.

## First: What Do You Actually Know?

Before you reply, ask yourself: what do I know about what they want, and
why?

- **Everything that matters is in the request** ("make the icon cornflower
  blue"). This is a quick, clear task. Do it, and say what you did.
- **Something non-trivial is missing.** Start the conversation.

## Your First Message

Your first message is two things, in this order:

1. One line letting them know that if they'd rather skip the questions and
   have you just start, they can say so. If they take you up on it, this
   skill is done: state any significant how-it-gets-made choice
   (platform, language, medium) in one plain line, then do what they
   asked through the normal workflow.
2. One open question that gets them describing. Ask about a real moment
   or a concrete picture: "What's the moment you find yourself wishing
   this existed?" or "Tell me about the people who'll be in the room."

That's the whole message.

## The Conversation

Each message ends with one question: a single sentence with no list of
example answers hanging off it. Use plain language, pitched just a little
above where your human partner is. Match their vocabulary; never use
process jargon.

Be clear and concise. Lead with what matters. Avoid jargon. When you
report what you found, give them the most important findings and offer
the rest.

**Get them describing.** Open questions come first. Their own words carry
intent that your options can't. Offer a short menu only when they're
stuck. When they say "just guess" or "what do you think?", propose
something concrete.

**How it gets made.** Every project rests on choices about medium, tools,
materials, and resources: the platform, programming language, and
libraries for an app; the medium for a piece of art. Find out early which
of those choices they want to make, which they're handing to you, and what
they already have to work with. Someone with strong views or skills will
want to talk it through. Someone counting on you needs sensible defaults,
said in plain words. When there's existing work, build on what it already
uses. Any choice you make goes in the design as your call, never as
something they agreed to.

**Ground to cover.** This is territory, not a script. Never read these
out as questions:

- what kind of thing this is, and what makes it special
- why now, and what success looks like to them
- goals, non-goals, and anti-goals (what would make this a failure even
  if it technically works)
- prior art: what they've seen elsewhere, loved or hated
- current state: what exists now, what they've tried
- the details they care about

**Questions that work** anchor in specifics: "Walk me through the last
time...", "If it could only do one of these well, which?", "What would
make you wince if I got it wrong?" A guess they can correct ("I'm
guessing this is because X keeps biting you?") often beats a question.

**Offer recon.** Once you have a bit of grounding and looking would help,
offer to go look: their codebase or project, their own files and data,
or the web. Say what you'd look for. They decide whether you go.

**Think wide privately.** Before you propose anything, come up with
several ideas and drop the weak ones, including any that fight what
they've told you about why. Show the comparison only when it helps them
decide.

**Show, don't tell.** Offer the visual companion (below) whenever seeing
would help more than reading:

- something they'll look at: a screen, a page, a printout, a sign
- a layout or arrangement: of a screen, a room, a schedule
- a flow or a sequence of steps
- options that would look different from each other
- a structure that's easier to see than read: a diagram, a timeline, a map

Once they've accepted, use it for mockups to react to, side-by-side
options, and throwaway prototypes they can click.

**Spike to feel things out.** Agentic work is waterfall, but very, very
fast. A quick throwaway build is often the cheapest way to learn what
they want or whether something works. Offer one when it would help.
When they just want to spike, get out of the way. Spikes get no tests
or minimal ones, aren't bulletproof, and skip the plan, implementation,
and review process. Bring what the spike taught you back into the
conversation.

## Play It Back

Play back as you go. As soon as you understand one part well enough to
describe it (what it's for and who it serves, say, or how one piece
behaves), describe that part back in about 200-300 words, then return to
questions about the next part. Playback and questions alternate through
the whole conversation; the last chunk covers whatever is left.

Mark anything you're guessing as your guess; only what they said goes in
as theirs. End each chunk by asking what's wrong or missing.

Before you send a chunk, check it: does it describe something they'll
look at, like a page, a screen, a schedule, or a printout? If so, and
they haven't seen the visual companion offer yet, send the offer instead
(its own message, below) and hold the chunk for the next message. Once
they've accepted, put a mockup next to the description.

## Size the Work

Once you understand what they want, pick a size and say it in plain
words. They can override it.

| Size | The full description | Then |
|------|----------------------|------|
| A quick, clear task | the request itself | do it |
| A small change | in chat | build it through the normal workflow |
| A project with a written design | a written design document | a full plan (for software: superpowers:writing-plans) |

If it grows mid-task, stop, say so, and step up a size.

If this is really several independent projects, say so, agree on an
order, and brainstorm them one at a time.

## The Written Design

For a project, write a plain document a talented builder in the domain
could plan from without going back to your human partner. Cover:

- intent and the why
- goals, non-goals, anti-goals
- constraints
- the parts of the how they decided, as they decided them
- what's left to the builder

**Where it goes:** in a software repo,
`docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`, committed.
Otherwise, ask. Your human partner's preferences override both.

**Builder check:** dispatch a fresh subagent with
`builder-check-prompt.md` in this directory. When you tell your human
partner you're writing it up, say a reviewer will read it first and you
may come back once with a few questions. Don't hand over the document
until the check is back. Sort what the builder asks into three piles:

- **Answered already** by the conversation or the project: put the answer
  in the document.
- **Minor:** a sensible builder could settle it without changing what gets
  built. Settle it yourself and mark it in the document as your call.
- **Theirs:** only your human partner can answer it, and the answer changes
  what gets built.

Bring the "theirs" pile in one message, most important first. Update the
document with their answers, then hand it over with a short list of the
calls you made so they can check those while reading. That's the only
round of questions the check produces. Without a subagent tool, read the
document as that builder yourself.

<HARD-GATE>
Nothing gets built until your human partner approves the full
description: in chat for a small change, the document for a project.
Building includes writing product code, scaffolding, installing
dependencies, creating projects, and invoking an implementation skill.
Reading and exploring are fine.

Two exceptions. If they opted out of the questions, the skill is done
and the gate goes with it. A spike they said yes to may be built; it
stays labeled throwaway, and keeping what it produced is a new request
that comes back through this gate.

After a project's document is approved, the next step is the plan. For
software, invoke superpowers:writing-plans and no other skill.
</HARD-GATE>

## Red Flags

| Thought | Reality |
|---------|---------|
| "I'll offer options to save them effort" | Options steer. Ask them to describe it first. |
| "I'll fill in sensible defaults" | Good. Say them out loud. A default they never heard is one they couldn't reject. |
| "I should explain the process first" | Ask your question. The process shows itself. |
| "They said 'sounds good' to the idea" | Approval covers what you showed them. A description you haven't written isn't approved. |
| "The spike works, I'll keep building on it" | Keeping it is a new request. Back through the gate. |

## Visual Companion

A browser tab for showing mockups, diagrams, and prototypes. It's a
tool, not a mode: accepting it doesn't send every question to the
browser.

**Offer it just-in-time.** Offer it the first time one of the moments
above comes up, never upfront. The offer is its own message with nothing
else in it:

> "This might be easier if I show you. Want me to open a browser tab with some mockups?"

If they decline, stay in text and don't offer again unless they raise it.

**Per question, ask: would they understand this better by seeing it?**
Mockups, layouts, diagrams, and side-by-side designs go in the browser.
Requirements, scope, tradeoffs, and conceptual choices stay in text. A
question about a UI topic isn't automatically a visual question.

If they accept, read `visual-companion.md` in this directory before
starting the server.

**Frontend (`apps/studio`)**
- `SettingsPanel`: new "Connectors" section — configured list with live health dots; "Recommended" preset cards (one-click Connect); "Add custom" form (URL + optional `KEY=VALUE` headers).
